title: Total influence bound for threshold representations
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{ -1,1 \\}$, and let $p$ be a real-valued function on that cube. Suppose that $f(x)$ is the sign of $p(x)$ for every $x$, with zero assigned the positive sign, and that $p(x)\\ne 0$ for every $x$. Then the total influence of the real-valued sign version of $f$ is at most the square root of $n$ plus the sum, over all coordinates, of the total influences of the threshold signs of the corresponding discrete derivatives of $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the two signs
$p$ is real-valued on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f(x)$ equals the threshold sign of $p(x)$ for every input
